title: Command Injection in Python
description: A server passes user input directly to an OS shell, letting an attacker run arbitrary commands on the host.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.description: User-supplied input reaches an OS shell interpreter without sanitization.
finding.why_dangerous: Shell=True lets the OS parse and execute attacker text like '; rm -rf /'.
finding.impact: Arbitrary command execution, full host compromise, data loss.
finding.fix: Avoid the shell entirely, pass an argument list, and validate the input with an allowlist.
learning_example: Input: host; whoami runs both ping and whoami
Parameterized subprocess.run([...]) treats input as a single argument

checklist: Never use shell=True with untrusted input
Pass command arguments as a list, not a string
Validate input with an allowlist of safe characters
Prefer standard library APIs over shell calls
Apply least privilege to the service account
